correctness.rationale: At a fixed time in a two-sided stationary rate-one Poisson process the backward age and successive interval lengths are independent unit exponentials. Brownian increments conditional on these lengths are independent Gaussians, so unconditionally the weighted contributions are independent centered Laplace variables c^jY_j of variance c^{2j}. The sum is square-summable in variance; translating the two-sided construction gives stationarity, while synchronous coupling contracts any initial difference by c^{N_t}→0 almost surely, including coalescence at the first reset for c=0. For χ_s(u)=1/(1+s²u²), χ_{b^j/√2}/χ_{a^j/√2}=q_j+(1−q_j)χ_{b^j/√2}, q_j=(a/b)^{2j}; the j=0 factor cancels. Centering and summability of b^{2j}−a^{2j} give the claimed almost-sure and L² convergence. The log-Laplace integral follows by differentiating in u, giving derivative −2s²u/(1+s²u²) and zero value at u=0. Integrating x² against each symmetric density difference yields b^{2j}−a^{2j}, proving Lévy integrability by a positive summable majorant; the sign is strictly positive, with the a=0 convention. The increment distributions compose by the transform ratios; consistent finite-dimensional distributions with an independent π₀ start yield the claimed process and centered increments give the natural-filtration martingale. Symmetric unimodality follows by convolution and limit of the Laplace laws. A shifted symmetric interval has probability no greater than at zero and has arbitrarily small probability sufficiently far away. Since the first nontrivial mixture term is unbounded with positive probability and independent of the rest, the average is strictly smaller for every r>0. Equivalently, conditional on common unit exponentials E_j, the stationary Gaussian variance V_c=Σ c^{2j}E_j increases strictly for a<b, so every such Gaussian central probability decreases strictly. Jensen gives both convex-order claims, with strictness for nondegenerate centered noise and strictly convex tests with finite expectations.
